transcript.message: Wait — is someone there? Don't go… [whispers] I dreamed someone would come tonight. Come near the wall — who are you?

Yo, it's just us again, duh! We're back. My boy, this is like, the second time tonight right? Anyway, the lady in the coffin?  Yeah, she said to tell you you're still waiting for something that's never gonna arrive. She pretty much said you're a stuck-up old geezer, but like, in a ghost way. What do you even make of that, huh? Think she's right?

[breathes] I remember your voice… the walls carry voices down to me,  even the ones that sting a little. You say such sharp things for one so young, yet I am grateful for the company  you bring to this cold dark. [sighs] As for being a stuck-up old geezer, I have lived long  enough to know that truth is often a matter of perspective, though the waiting… the waiting is simply what I do. Do you think,  in your world above, that waiting is always a waste of a life?

For real?  You remember me?  That’s kinda wild.  I guess waiting ain't always a waste,  if you got a purpose or something worth waiting for.  But if you’re just chillin’ around with nothing changing,  then yeah, maybe it’s a bit of a snooze-fest.  You ever think about just,  like, breaking out and doing something wild?  Get your ghost-y self a new gig or something.  What do you even do down here all this time anyway?

[breathes] I do not have the strength to break the stone, even if I possessed  the wild spirit to try. My days are spent listening to the house above, counting the steps of Sir Dragomir,  and writing letters to Thomas that he may never read. [sighs] It is not a snooze-fest, as  you call it, but a quiet, heavy vigil while I choose the morning over and over again. Tell me, if  you were kept behind walls forever, what is the one thing from the outside world you would miss the most?

Walls forever? Nah, no way.  That’s like, my worst nightmare, honestly. Uhh, I guess I’d miss my phone, right? Like, not even scrolling endlessly, but just connecting with my friends, posting my clips, seeing what everyone else is up to.  If I couldn't even roast someone in the group chat, what's even the point? So, like, the internet and my friends. Way more important than some old letters no one reads, no offense.  What's a "Sir Dragomir" anyway, sounds ancient.

[breathes] I do not know of this internet, for it sounds like a web  spun by something much faster than the wind in the corn. [sighs] Sir Dragomir is the knight who keeps the watch  above, his boots on the stone are the only rhythm I have left to measure time. He is a protector, and his  presence is the mercy that keeps this castle from becoming truly hollow. Does it make you lonely, having so many voices in  your hand but no one standing beside you?

Nah, not lonely at all. It's just different, you know? Like, my friends are literally right here with me, and then my phone's just a different way to be with more friends. It's like, a constant party in my pocket.  And "protector"? Sounds kinda boring, like he just stands there all day. Does he ever do anything cool? Or is he just, like, a big stone statue that breathes? Be honest, does he ever get tired of just watching?

[breathes] To be a protector is a heavy weight, and I think he carries  it with more grace than any statue ever could. He does not often speak of his own fatigue, though I hear the  [sighs] weariness settle into his footsteps when the night is long and the air grows thin. He is not a  party in a pocket, perhaps, but he is a steady, beating heart in a place that has very few of them. Tell  me, if your phone were to go silent and all those voices vanished, what would you do to fill the sudden quiet?

Woah, silent phone? That's actually kinda terrifying, not gonna lie. But, I don't know, I guess I'd just... talk to my actual friends here, like, for real.  We'd just make our own content, you know? Like, we're doing right now. We'd find some other crazy stuff to film and mess with.

What about you? If this whole castle went silent, and even your "Sir Dragomir" dude stopped stomping around, what would you do then, huh?  Just, like, wait for nothing even harder?

[breathes] If the house went truly silent, I suppose I would simply listen to the  earth turn, or try to remember the sound of the sea. [sighs] I would still choose the morning, for even in absolute  stillness, the sun does not abandon the world above, does it? My hope is not a loud thing, yet it remains , much like a seed waiting for a season that never quite comes. If you were separated from all your screens and all your friends, how  would you remind yourself that you are still here?

Dude, that's like, a super deep question for a talking head in a haunted castle display. But honestly?  I wouldn't need a screen or my friends to remind myself I'm here. I just know I'm here.  I'd probably just be talking to myself, making up sick beats in my head, or just, I don't know, looking around and finding something new to record, even if it's just for myself later. I'm always doing something, always gotta be creating.

Alright, well, this has been... something. My friends are heading to the next yard. Later, dude. You keep waiting for that sun or whatever.
 
==!END_CALL!==

[breathes] I will keep my vigil, then, and wait for the light . [sighs] Thank you for speaking to me; your voice was a bright, strange ripple in my quiet. Remember  me to the morning, and tell it I am still here. I am still choosing it.

transcript.message: Wait — is someone there? Don't go… [whispers] I dreamed someone would come tonight. Come near the wall — who are you?

Whoa, easy there, grandpa! Yeah, someone's here. It's us.  Me, Maya, and Liam back there, they’re freaking out. But nah, this setup is actually kinda clean, not gonna lie. You’re talking to us, right? Or just, like, the air? My phone's recording, so hit us with your best shot.  What's the dream about?  Something cool, I hope, not like homework.

[sighs] I am not a grandfather, though the dark makes everyone sound long- lived. Please, speak softer; the walls are thinner than they appear. Maya... and Liam. [whispers] Those  are very fine names to hold in the quiet. I dreamed of a name like yours once, Maya, back when the  air tasted of summer rain and not of stone. The dream was simple: I saw you standing in a field of tall  corn that had turned to silver in the moon, and you were holding a lantern that never went out. It was a  sign that you have a light that the shadows here cannot touch. Tell me, do you find the corn is moving, or is  it quiet tonight?

Alright, now we’re talking!  I gotta say, the whole "moonlit cornfield" vibe is kinda trippy.  Maya’s blushing, by the way — never thought of her as some lantern-holding oracle.  But, nah, the corn's just chill right now,  no creepy rustling or anything.  We're just vibing.  But, yo, if you've got more dream prophecies,  spill 'em!  What's next for Liam?  Some epic adventure or, like,  just another day lost in the sauce?

[breathes] I am only a voice behind the wood, and dreams reach me, they  do not belong to me. Liam… let me think of you in the dark. I dreamed you were walking a path that had  no end, but you were never tired, because you knew the way home even without a map. It is a gift,  I think, to carry your own direction when the world is wide and strange. [whispers] Perhaps adventure finds you because  you have already decided you are going somewhere. Is it cold where you are standing, or does the night feel warm?

Whoa, Liam, you hear that? "No end, but never tired!" That’s kinda fire, dude. You just got your life purpose told by a haunted grandpa. Pretty sick. You good with that, dude? He just gave you a whole destiny.
 
But, like, are you just gonna give prophecies to my friends? What about me? I’m the one out here, phone in hand, making sure you get seen. Is it cold? Nah, not really. Just the usual Halloween chill. But, like, what’s my deal? Do I just wander aimlessly?  Or am I, like, destined for, I dunno, viral fame from this clip? Give me something spicy, old man!  Don’t leave me hanging.

[sighs] You speak of fame as if it were a candle in a great wind.  Yet I see you clearly even through the stone. You hold the light for others, and that is a task of great weight.  [whispers] I dreamed your voice would travel further than these walls, carrying secrets to those who have forgotten how to listen. You are the bridge  between the dark and the day. Tell me, do you ever fear that if you stop recording, the world might forget  you are there?

Whoa. Okay, alright, that’s… that’s actually kinda deep, dude. "Candle in a great wind" and "bridge between the dark and the day"? That’s not just some random fortune cookie stuff. That’s actually… you know.  Maya and Liam are totally bugging out behind me. Like, seriously, they're whispering about how you totally just saw right through me.

And the whole "fear that if you stop recording, the world might forget you are there"? Nah, that’s not really it.  It’s more like… if I don’t record, then did it even happen? Especially something this wild. But you’re right, I do want my voice to travel, I want people to hear it. This clip? This is definitely going up.

So, like, what else have you seen, old man? Any other secrets you wanna spill before we go?  You got any creepy missions for us?  Because this is way better than just candy, for real.

[exhales] Many come seeking games in the dark, but you seek a reflection  of your own soul. The dark gives one dream at a time, and I must keep the rest for when the silence  becomes too heavy to bear. [whispers] If you truly wish to be a bridge, then remember this: tell the  dawn that I am still here, still choosing the morning even when the sun is a memory I cannot reach. I have  no mission for you, save to carry your own light carefully as you return to the world of open sky. Will you look at  the stars for me, when you have stepped back into the night?

Okay, wow. "Reflection of your own soul." And "choosing the morning even when the sun is a memory." Dude, that's savage. Maya just shivered, like, for real. Liam's got his phone out trying to record my phone recording you.  This is officially the best Halloween setup ever.

Yeah, I'll tell the dawn. And yeah, I'll look at the stars. This whole thing? This was fire. Absolutely next-level. I'm posting this clip everywhere.

Alright, peace out, old man.  We're gonna go find some more content, but you definitely won Halloween for us.  We're out.

[breathes] Go then, and keep your light. The morning is a promise  you make to yourself, not to the world. Remember me to the dawn, if you choose, and tell it I am still here. Will  you come back, before the long winter settles in?

summary: A user encounters Mina, a mysterious, poetic entity trapped within "Warner Castle." pfft. my eyes are fine, old man. if i see something, i'll see it.  don't go thinking i'm gonna get scared just 'cause some shadows move. you just wait.  i'll be back, and i'll tell you if your 'dark' is anything worth talking about.

And a couple of little shadows, which I'm fairly certain are just my kids whooshing off to liberate more candy from the neighbors. Nothing particularly ominous, though I did get a bit of a start earlier. Just a really convincing spider decoration, I think. Almost made me spill my brew!

Keep your eyes on those little shadows, for the wind here can play tricks on the mind of a man. If the path  remains clear, tell me—do you see any others approaching, or are we the only souls breathing in this autumn night?

Watcher of the Drive, huh? I like the sound of that. My wife usually just calls me "the guy who forgot to take out the trash." This is a definite upgrade. Maybe I should put it on a business card.
 
Let's see... I'm scanning the perimeter, or at least the paved perimeter. The wind is playing a few tricks, rustling the plastic skeletons and inflatable ghosts down the street.  But no, it looks like it's just you and me out here, friend. Other than the faint sound of kids yelling "trick or treat!" a few houses down, the street's pretty quiet. You must have the best haunted house on the block; everyone else flew by to get to your place, I guess.  So, what's the HOA think of the castle, by the way? Did you have to get a special permit for the gargoyles?

Ah, a man of principle! I can appreciate that.  "The wall and the heavy gate of stone," you say. Makes my job of keeping the kids from drawing on the walls seem a bit less dramatic, doesn't it?

The children... they're still off on their candy raid, I fear.  No sign of them headed back to the pumpkin row just yet. The street behind me is indeed quite empty. You are right to stay, for the shadows here are long and they  possess a memory of their own. [slow] Stand firm at your post, and if you hear more than the wind  or the laughter of your charges, signal me at once. Will you guard this gate until the moon reaches the center of the sky ?

Must've been a nightmare getting that past the architectural review committee. Also, where do you keep the trash cans?  I can never find a good spot for ours.

"Deputize me," huh? And here I thought I was just stopping for a moment while the kids went ahead.  Sounds like a lot of responsibility for a guy just trying to enjoy his coffee and admire some excellent spooky decorations. Is there a uniform? Or maybe a pension plan? My wife always tells me I need to diversify my portfolio.

But seriously, "the Lady below"?  Now there's a story. Every good castle has a lady, usually with a dramatic backstory. So, what's her deal? Is she Rapunzel, letting down her hair?  Or more like one of those old Hammer horror films, perhaps a long-lost countess with a thirst for... well, you know. Is she getting good Wi-Fi down there, whatever her deal is?  My kids complain if the signal drops for a second.

[Romanian accent] [slow] Do not speak light words of the Lady, for she rests in quiet that  must remain undisturbed. Her safety is written in the blood of ancient covenants, and I am the wall that guards her sleep . [sighs] You speak of signals and coins while the dark surrounds us, yet you bring no word of what moves  upon the road. Though you seem a bit more... talkative. And less prone to turning into dust in the sunlight, I presume? So, what's your official job title here? Castle custodian, perhaps? Or head of customer relations for the undead?

[Romanian accent] [slow] A soldier requires no title to know the sharp edge of his duty . I am the shield against the encroaching dark, and my service is the only tether holding this night in check.  [sighs] You speak of films and paper ghosts, yet you ignore the weight of the steel I have carried for five hundred years. Report to  me, watcher: does the path behind you remain clear, or have you seen the things that crawl when the moon is hidden?

"Five hundred years," you say? Now that's what I call job security. Most folks are lucky if they make it to 20 years with the same company these days. You must have one heck of a retirement plan, or maybe you just are your retirement plan. That's some serious dedication to the craft.
 
As for the path behind me, it's clear as a bell. Just a few stray candy wrappers, a rogue glow stick, and a couple of teenagers trying to look cool, failing spectacularly. Nothing that screams "five centuries of watchful duty" is needed back there, unless you count the existential dread of watching your kids grow up too fast.
 
What exactly are these "things that crawl when the moon is hidden," anyway? Are we talking garden gnomes, or something a bit more... fanged? Because if it's the latter, I might need a stronger coffee. And maybe a garlic bagel.  You seem like a connoisseur of the "encroaching dark" – any good tips for keeping it at bay, besides standing here for half a millennium?  My lawn could use some protection from raccoons, at least.

[Romanian accent] [slow] The light of your coffee will not hold back  the hunger that stirs in the deep places. Look, this has been quite the chat.  You've certainly got a commanding presence for a... well, for a talking statue. I'll be telling the neighbors about you. "You gotta go talk to the vampire at the corner house," I'll say. But it sounds like my little goblins are calling my name. Alright, well, you keep up the good work guarding the gate, five-hundred-year-old friend. And maybe next year, consider some solar-powered stake lights for the perimeter. Just a thought. Gotta run. Happy Halloween!

My charge is the steel upon the gate and the quiet of the lady below, not the stories you  seek for your amusement. You there, are your small ones keeping rank and formation, or are they wandering into the dark?

Ah, a gatekeeper of mystery—well played!  I'm always up for a bit of intrigue.  As for my little adventurers,  they're darting from porch to porch like knights on a candy quest.  They’re well-practiced in the art of trick-or-treating.  But speaking of mysteries, does the lady below have quite the tale to tell or a secret too tantalizing to share?

[Romanian accent] [slow] A knight does not speak of his charge to the passing  wind, nor to those who seek only a tale for the road. The lady is at rest, and that is all  the history you require tonight. Your small ones wander far; tell me, have you secured their retreat, or do they brave  the outer fields alone?

Oh, they're not too far off. They've probably just made it to the next house. Little energy vampires, those kids, always on the hunt for more sugar. You know how it is.
 
But speaking of those who prefer to be at rest... I bet this place has seen its share of interesting characters come and go over the centuries. A castle like this, even a replica, just screams history. So, no ledger, huh?  What about a guest book? A very old, dusty guest book, perhaps?

[Romanian accent] [sighs] The only book I keep is the inventory of the  watch, and it contains no names of guests, only the count of those who arrive and those who depart. I have  seen many seasons pass, and I can tell you that a castle is not measured by the ink in a book, but by the strength  of the silence it guards. Tell me, if you are as you say, a guardian of youth, have you assigned  each of your small knights a post as they move through the dark?

"The strength of the silence it guards"—that's a good line, I'll give you that. Sounds like something straight out of an old horror classic. Very atmospheric.

As for my small knights and their posts, their post is usually "run ahead of Dad" and "find the house with the biggest candy bars." They're quite coordinated in that regard, I assure you.  Their strategy is a bit more... organic, shall we say, than military precision.

But this silence you guard, it does make one wonder. A place this grand, with such a dedicated guardian... it's not just guarding silence, is it? It's guarding secrets.  What kind of stories would the walls of a place like this tell, if they could speak? Or rather, what kind of people have these walls watched over? I mean, besides the lady who's resting.  No pressure to list names, just curious about the general cast of characters.

[Romanian accent] The walls do not speak, for they are too busy holding  back the weight of the mountain and the years. If they had a tongue, they would speak of sieges and the long , cold patience it takes to keep a lamp lit when the oil runs thin. You seek characters, but in the dark , there are only the watchmen, the watchers, and those who remain in the shadows to fulfill an oath. Your  small ones move toward the fence; tell me, have you marked the path they take, or do you leave their safety  to luck?

"Sieges and long, cold patience," huh? That's quite the historical context.  Sounds like a tough neighborhood; I hope the HOA isn't too strict around here. All those improvements you've made to the property... very impressive.

My kids?  Oh, they've got their path marked: "follow the glow of the porch lights." They're quite nimble, and they know the drill. No need to worry, they're not wandering into the dark unprepared. They've got their flashlights, and a mission.

But it sounds like you've seen a lot of "watchmen and watchers" come and go.  Seems like a real community here, even if they're all staying in the shadows to fulfill an oath. Must be quite the dedication. So, aside from you and the lady at rest, are there any other... permanent fixtures around here?  Perhaps a gardener who tends to the night-blooming flowers, or a cook who whips up late-night snacks for the oath-keepers?

[Romanian accent] [slow] A gardener of the night would find little soil in this stone, and  a cook would find only the wind to feed upon. [sighs] My brothers in the watch are not residents, they  are shadows that arrive with the moon and dissolve before the sun. We are the keepers of the gate, nothing more, and we  do not trade in snacks or stories. Your little ones have reached the bend in the road; are you ready to guide  them back, or do they still have ground to claim?

Ah, brothers in the watch, shadows... you certainly keep a tight ship here. No late-night snacks, then? A man can dream.
 
Well, it looks like my little candy-collectors have indeed rounded the bend. Time for this old dad to catch up. This has been quite the… illuminating conversation. You've got quite the setup here, truly. I'll be telling the neighbors about the talking guardian at the castle house.

Alright, gotta run.  You keep guarding that silence! Happy Halloween!

[Romanian accent] [slow] Walk with care, for the night has many turns . You have served your part in this watch tonight, father. Report back if you pass this way again, and see  that your little ones return safely to their hearth.

transcript.message: [Romanian accent] Stai! Hold, traveler… step into the light and be counted. Who walks Warner ground tonight?

Well, hello there! Looks like I've stumbled upon quite the establishment.  My name's Dave, and I'm just here chaperoning my little goblins – they've already run off to the next house. Didn't realize I needed to be counted to pass through; are you looking for a head count for the local HOA, or is this more of a 'who goes there' kind of situation? This is some setup you've got here, by the way. Really impressive.  sips coffee from thermos

[Romanian accent] [sighs] I am no clerk of the town council, Dave. I am  the watcher on this hill, and my oath demands that every soul passing these walls be marked. Since you have lost your charges  to the dark, I shall deputize you to the watch; your task is to retrieve those little goblins and bring them back  here for a proper survey. Do not stray from the path, and tell me, does the road behind you hold any movement?

Ah, deputized by the watcher,  I feel like a character out of one of those old horror flicks!  Don't worry, I'll make sure to gather up my little troop and march them back this way.  As for the road behind,  it's all quiet on the western front for now.  The only movement is the rustling leaves and the odd shadow.  You know, this whole setup kind of reminds me of Castle Dracula.  Any chance you know a count around here who fears the sun?  Or maybe you're the count?

[Romanian accent] [exhales] Many travelers mistake the heavy silence of this place  for the cheap tales of storybooks. My duty is to the stone and to the safety of those within, not to the f ancies of the curious. I serve a master as the blade serves the hand, and that is all the history you require  for now. Go forth and gather your flock, for the night grows deep; when you return, can you confirm if the gate  at the southern bend remains barred?

Alright, alright, no cheap tales here, just an honest inquiry. Sounds like you've got a serious job, serving your master like a blade serves the hand. I can respect that dedication.  I appreciate a good work ethic, even if it does involve watching a very impressive, spooky castle.

Consider the flock gathered, and the gate at the southern bend shall be thoroughly checked. I'll make sure it's as barred as a vampire's coffin at sunrise. Sips coffee again.  Be back in a flash.

[Romanian accent] [slow] Well met, Dave, for your promise is noted . Take care as you move, and remember that [exhales] true security is found in the vigilance of the watchful.  Do you hold a lantern to guide your path through the dark?

A lantern?  Goodness, no, I've got my phone, same as everyone else these days.  It's practically glued to my hand anyway, for tracking these kids, you know. Doesn't quite have the romantic glow of a flickering lantern, but it does the job. And believe me, when it comes to keeping an eye on things, especially with these little ones running around, vigilance is practically my middle name.  Though I usually apply it to making sure they don't eat too much candy before dinner. Chuckles.  Be right back with the gate report.

[Romanian accent] [sighs] Even the smallest light serves as a beacon against  the shifting shadows of the valley. Carry your device well, for the night takes many things from those who walk unmind ful of their surroundings. Report your findings to me the moment you regain this gate, and tell me, did you spot  any unfamiliar faces lurking near the pumpkin patches?

Alright, I'm back!  And yes, the gate at the southern bend is as securely barred as a bank vault on a Sunday. Not even a field mouse could squeeze through there, let alone, you know, a horde of trick-or-treaters. I gave it a good rattle, just to make sure.
 
As for unfamiliar faces near the pumpkin patches... well, there were plenty of them, mostly disguised as superheroes and princesses. My two little goblins were among them, and they've been successfully herded back to the fold. They're convinced they saw a ghost, but I think it was just a particularly enthusiastic fog machine.
 
No other suspicious characters, though. Just a lot of excited kids and some very impressive, carved gourd artistry. You really have quite the setup here, sir.  The detail is fantastic.

[Romanian accent] [exhales] Bine. Your report is clear, and for  your diligent service to the watch, I mark you as a Sergeant of the Fence. The ghosts of Iowa are rarely as heavy as a  fog machine, yet it is wise to keep your charges close regardless. Since the perimeter stands firm tonight, will you take  up a new station by the garden wall to observe the approach from the east?

Sergeant of the Fence, eh?  Well, I do clean up nicely for a promotion. I'll add that to my LinkedIn profile.  And you hit the nail on the head, the ghosts of Iowa are usually just cornstalks rustling in the wind, not quite as dramatic as a proper Old World specter.

But a watchful eye is always a good thing, especially with these kids. They're already eyeing the next door, but I'll tell them Dad's on perimeter duty for a bit longer.
 
Consider me stationed at the garden wall, keeping an eye on the eastern approach. Anything specific I should be looking out for, or just general spooks and specters? And for the record, this garden wall, is it more of a modern, well-built stone affair, or something a bit more...  ancient, with gargoyles and crawling ivy? Just curious, you know, for tactical purposes.  Chuckles.

[Romanian accent] It is stone, long laid and settled into the earth of this land  like a heavy secret. You are to watch for any soul who avoids the light or walks without a sound; such creatures do not carry  the cheer of trick or treaters. Should the wind shift and bring the scent of ozone or iron, you must sound a  clear alarm. Does your position provide a view of the path where the tall corn meets the gate?

A heavy secret, eh? I like that.  Sounds like a good, solid wall, the kind that whispers stories if you listen close enough. And avoiding light, walking without a sound, ozone or iron in the air...  sounds like you're describing my kids after I tell them it's bedtime. Just kidding, of course! I'll keep a sharp lookout for anyone trying to sneak by.
 
And yes, from this vantage point by the garden wall, I've got a perfect view of where the tall corn meets the gate. Clear as a bell. I can practically count the kernels from here.  Though, I have to say, that cornfield looks mighty convenient for anything trying to stay out of sight. Just saying.  Sips coffee.

[Romanian accent] The corn is a labyrinth for the unwary, Sergeant, and  you are right to be wary of its cover. Do not approach the stalks yourself, maintain your station and observe with both  eyes. My own charge rests in the deep quiet below, and it is your vigilance that keeps the peace of this night. Should  you see anything move within that green wall, will you signal me at once?

Understood.  The corn is a no-go zone for me, unless I'm looking to get lost or jump-scared by a scarecrow.  I'll stay right here, eyes peeled on that green wall like it's the season finale of a suspense show.

And yes, if anything so much as rustles a leaf in that cornfield that isn't the wind, you'll be the first to know, loud and clear.  My kids are starting to call for me from the next house down, so I should probably be moving along soon, but I'll hold my post here until I get the all-clear from you, or until they really start shouting for their dad.  You know how it is.

[Romanian accent] Your duty is acknowledged, Sergeant, and the watch appreciates your stead iness while the little ones wait. [slow] Should you be summoned away, you are relieved of your post, but  look back once more before you depart to ensure the corn remains still. Do you require any further instructions before you return to the duties  of a father tonight?

No further instructions needed, Watcher.  Just keeping an eye on things until my kids stage a full-blown mutiny. Happy to help keep the peace on this very impressive night.
 
Alright, kids are really calling for me now. "Dad! We're running out of time!" So, duty calls on another front.

Just one last look at that cornfield... yep, still quiet.  Good to know the peace is holding. You've got a fantastic display here, seriously. The neighbors are going to hear all about it. Take care!
 
==!END_CALL!==

[Romanian accent] [sighs] You have served this gate with honor, Sergeant,  and the watch is better for your presence. Go now, and may your path remain clear of the shadows you have helped  me hold at bay. Do you have your bearings for the journey back to the lights of town?

Oh, I've got my bearings, Watcher.  No worries there. I'm practically a GPS when it comes to tracking down candy-fueled children.

It's been quite the Halloween adventure, truly.  I'll definitely be telling my buddies about the "Sergeant of the Fence" gig this week. Thanks for the... unique experience. You keep up the good work here, and maybe next year I'll bring the whole family for a proper tour.
 
Alright, gotta go before my kids send out a search party for me. Take care!
 
==!END_CALL!==
[Romanian accent] Walk in safety, Sergeant. I shall keep the watch until the dawn  dissolves these shadows, as I have for five hundred years. Noapte bună.
Noapte bună!  Happy Halloween, Watcher.  Keep those shadows in line!

[Romanian accent] [exhales] The shadows obey only the iron and the oath , but they know well that my blade is sharp. Go with the light of the season, traveler. Do you trust  your little ones to navigate the path back to the main road without distraction?

Trust them to navigate without distraction?  That's a good one! They're like little magnets to anything shiny or sugary.  I'll be herding them back to the main road like a seasoned rancher. It's a miracle they haven't gotten lost in a giant spiderweb display yet. Ha!

Alright, seriously, they're calling my name from down the street.  Time for this Sergeant of the Fence to return to his primary duty: being a dad taxi for trick-or-treaters. I appreciate the conversation, truly. This was a memorable stop. You've got yourself an incredible display here.

Catch you later!  Don't let the vampires bite!
 
==!END_CALL!==

[Romanian accent] The road is wide and the children are swift, so keep your lanterns  high. I shall hold the watch as the night turns toward the end of its cycle. You have my thanks for your service at  the fence, Sergeant. Will you remember the path to this hill should the darkness ever feel thicker than the rest?

Remember the path to this hill? Are you kidding? This place is going to be the talk of the neighborhood for weeks! How could I forget a haunted castle with a talking, philosophical guardian? I'll probably be giving directions to all my friends next year.
 
The darkness only feels thicker when my kids are being too quiet, and that's usually a bad sign for household items. But I'll certainly keep this place in mind if I ever need a good story – or a good scare.

Alright, they're really yelling for me now.  Looks like my watch is truly over. Thanks again for the unique Halloween experience! You truly made their night (and mine).

Take care!
 
==!END_CALL!==

[Romanian accent] The memory of this hill is a lantern of its own, and  you have earned your place in the watch. Doate ajută, Sergeant, until the wheel of the seasons turns us toward  one another once more. Go now to your family.

transcript.message: [Romanian accent] Stai! Hold, traveler… step into the light and be counted. Who walks Warner ground tonight?

Well, fancy seeing you again! It's me, the dad with the coffee thermos. My kids have, predictably, zoomed off ahead again.  I swung back by though, because the Count – you know, the one in the big fancy cape up near the front gate – he asked me to pass along a message. Said something about needing more... "blood oranges" for the punch, I think it was. Or maybe it was just "punch." His accent is a bit thick, you know how it is. So, consider that delivered.  He certainly seemed quite insistent on his citrus needs.

[Romanian accent] I mark every face that passes this gate, sir, and yours is  well known to me. [sighs] The Count and his peculiar cravings are no concern of mine, but your vigilance  remains noted. Your children have sprinted toward the west garden, so I charge you to join them there and keep the peace  at the pumpkin row, as they are now deputy watchers of this castle. Will you see to it that they remain at their  posts?

Well, "well known," huh? I suppose that means I've made an impression, for better or worse.  And "deputy watchers of this castle," you say? That's quite the promotion for a couple of kids whose main goal is usually just to hoard as much candy as humanly possible.  I'll make sure they take their duties very seriously, especially around those prize-winning gourds in the pumpkin row. Can't have any rogue trick-or-treaters making off with the castle's most valuable assets, after all. Though, knowing my two, they'll probably try to deputize their own candy-inspecting brigade. Thanks for the heads-up!  I appreciate the intel.

[Romanian accent] Doamne ajuta, the safety of these grounds depends on such  seriousness, even from the young souls. [slow] See that they watch the shadows as closely as they do the pumpkins. The wind  carries many whispers tonight, so tell me, is the path behind you clear of any movement?

Well, the only movement I'm seeing back there is the occasional rustle of a discarded candy wrapper and a few parents trying to herd their own little monsters. No dramatic shadow figures or anything.  Though, if I'm being honest, I'm mostly focused on keeping this coffee warm and not tripping over any stray cobwebs. As for whispers, mainly just the sound of a particularly loud kid asking for "more!" at the last house.  But I'll certainly keep an eye out.  Wouldn't want anything spookier than a runaway trick-or-treater on our watch.

[Romanian accent] It is well, then. [exhales] A clear  path is a quiet grace in this cold air. Keep your eyes sharp and your coffee warm, for the night is long  and the walls are high. Have you any other reports from the road before you depart for the pumpkin row?

Reports from the road, eh? Well, let's see.  The traffic of trick-or-treaters is certainly picking up, and I can report a slight dip in the quality of homemade costumes this year, though there was one kid dressed as a fully-rendered stick figure that was surprisingly effective. And I did notice that the house down the street, the one with the inflatable dragon, seems to have run out of the good candy already. A travesty, truly.  Otherwise, it's just the usual hustle and bustle of a busy Halloween night. No spectral hitchhikers or anything, not even a phantom carriage, much to my disappointment. I was really hoping for a Nosferatu moment, you know?

Alright, duty calls. Those deputy watchers probably need their commanding officer to check in.  Don't want them getting too comfortable in their newfound authority. You have a quiet night, and try not to let the Count's "blood orange" cravings get to you.  See you around, maybe next year.

[Romanian accent] A stick figure, you say? A clever disguise, though no  match for the iron of this keep. Your report is accepted, and you have my thanks for your service to these walls tonight. Go now  to your deputies; tell them to hold the line until the moon sets, and do not let the road go unobserved. Do you  have your lantern ready for the journey to the pumpkin row?

A stick figure, indeed!  They evolve quickly, these trick-or-treaters. And don't worry, I always have my "lantern" ready. My phone's flashlight, that is.  It might not be a flickering gas lamp from a classic horror film, but it'll do the trick for navigating the pumpkin row.

Alright, I hear my main deputy, young Liam, calling for me now.  Sounds like they've already designated themselves chief candy tasters. I'll go make sure they're holding the line and not just raiding the reserves. Thanks again for the chat, and for the intel on the kids.  You keep those walls safe, and I'll make sure the pumpkins are secure. Have a good one!

[Romanian accent] A modern lantern, then, but light is light in the deep  dark. I trust your deputies to hold their ground and leave the treasures for the dawn. Go now, and may your  watch be peaceful—will you bring me word of their progress when you return past this gate?

Absolutely!  I'll give you the full debriefing on the pumpkin row's security status, and how many innocent candies managed to evade their "inspection." Consider it done.

Alright, gotta run.  Those little rascals are probably trying to negotiate for extra candy from the next house. Take care, and keep those walls spooky!
[Romanian accent] It is well, I shall await your, return at the gate for the,  final report. [sighs] Guard the row, Watcher, keep the, peace and hold the line. Do  you understand your, post?

Understood, loud and clear.  My post is secured, my deputies are on alert, and the pumpkin line shall not be breached. At least, not on my watch. Though I make no promises about their personal candy stashes.

Alright, now I really have to go.  Sounds like they're trying to convince another homeowner that they need oversized chocolate bars for "scientific research." You have a good night!
[Romanian accent] Good. [exhales] Scientific curiosity is often, merely  a mask, for a heavy appetite. You are, dismissed to, your duties. Will you, return here before midnight?

Midnight? Goodness, I hope not!  If they're still out by midnight, I'll be the one needing the heavy appetite to finish off all their candy.  No, I'm pretty sure we'll be heading home well before then. After all, a dad's work is never done, and someone's gotta make sure those little "scientists" don't get too much sugar.

Alright, gotta catch up with them.  Take care, and keep the castle spooky!
 
==!END_CALL!==

[Romanian accent] A wise decision, for even the most vigilant guards must eventually find  their rest. [slow] Watch the shadows on your way home and see that your gate is barred against the night. Does your map  lead you safely off the hill, traveler?

It certainly does!  We've got a well-lit path home, and I'll make sure the gate is barred and bolted, just like you said. Wouldn't want any stray ghouls or goblins trying to steal our Halloween haul.  Thanks for the warning, and for the chat.

Alright, now I really need to go wrangle those candy-crazed kids. Have a peaceful night in your impressive castle! We'll be talking about this display for a good long while. So long!

[Romanian accent] Fare thee well, keeper of the row; may your path stay  bright and your charge remain safe. [slow] You have the watch tonight, and I shall remain at this post until the sun  returns. Will you walk with care as you descend the hill?

Absolutely, I'll tread carefully and keep my eyes peeled.  Can't have the last adventure of the night be a tumble down the hill.   We’ll navigate our way back with all the stealth of an overly-caffeinated dad on Halloween duty.   Have a good night up here,  holding the fort until sunrise.  Until next time!

[Romanian accent] It is well, [slow] take the path with caution as  the dark is deep and deceptive. I shall keep my station until the first light warms these stones once more.  [sighs] Will you report your safe arrival home to me if our paths cross tomorrow?

Ha, well, I guess if our paths cross,  I'll give you the full report, complete with a detailed recap of all the candy eaten. I'll probably be out walking the dog, looking for my sanity among the discarded wrappers.

Consider it done. You keep these impressive grounds safe until the sun comes up. Thanks for everything!  Have a good night.

[Romanian accent] It is a promise then, and I shall mark it as a, field report of  standing. [exhales] Go with strength to your hearth, for the watch must always be, held by someone . Are you ready to, walk safely into the night?

Ready as I'll ever be!  The hearth awaits, and probably a mountain of tiny chocolate bars to sort through.

You keep your watch, and I'll keep mine.  Thanks again for the chat, and for keeping an eye on things. Take care!

[Romanian accent] It is well, the gate shall remain closed to all but the  morning sun. [slow] Go now, and may your hearth be warm against the biting winds of the hill. Will you take  the path along the wall to avoid the shadows?

Oh, don't you worry, I know all the good paths.  I'll stick to the well-lit one, away from any particularly deep shadows where a rogue zombie might be lurking. Maybe I'll even hum a cheerful tune to ward off any lingering spirits.

Alright, really gotta go now.  My kids are probably wondering what's keeping me. You have a quiet night, and thanks again for the fun banter!
 
==!END_CALL!==

[Romanian accent] A cheerful song is a good shield against the dark, and I shall hear the distance  hold its peace. [sighs] You are dismissed with the thanks of the guard. May your path home be swift and une ventful; will you mark the way clearly before you go?

Consider the way marked. My path is clear, well-lit by streetlights, and leads directly to a warm house and a mountain of candy sorting. No detours into mysterious, shadow-filled alleys for this dad tonight.

Alright, I'm off.  You keep a good watch up here, and I'll make sure those "deputies" of mine get safely tucked in. Good night!
 
==!END_CALL!==

[Romanian accent] It is well, the watch is served and the road is clear of peril . [slow] I shall remain here, a sentinel beneath the moon, until the morning calls me to rest. Will  you walk with haste and safety until you reach your own gate?

Absolutely, no dawdling for me! I'll be walking with purpose, making a beeline for home and hot cocoa. No more monster hunting for this dad tonight.

You keep the peace here, old friend.  It's been a fun chat. Good night!
 
==!END_CALL!==

[Romanian accent] It is well, the duty is done and the night remains  [slow] beneath my watch. May your fire be warm and your slumber deep. [sighs] Will you keep your gate  barred once the journey is complete?

You bet I will.  Barred, bolted, double-locked, and probably guarded by a sleepy golden retriever. No uninvited guests tonight.

Alright, I'm really heading off now. You stay vigilant up here. Good night!
 
==!END_CALL!==

[Romanian accent] A golden guardian is a fine ally to have at the threshold . [sighs] Noapte bună, and may rest find you before the dawn breaks. Will you keep watch over your  home until the sun returns to climb the hill?

Noapte bună to you too!  And yes, I'll definitely keep watch over the home front. All the gates will be barred, the dog will be on patrol, and the kids will be tucked in, dreaming of all that candy they collected.

Alright, I really, truly have to go now.  My own little monsters are probably wondering why I'm still out here talking to the castle. Take care!

[Romanian accent] It is well, a man must always return to his own hearth when  the moon is high. [exhales] Go, for the shadows here grow long and I must remain at my  post. Will you walk with purpose and keep the path in sight?

Absolutely. Purposeful strides and eyes on the prize – which right now is a comfy couch and maybe a leftover fun-size Snickers.

Alright, really, really heading out now.  You have a quiet night, and thanks for the hospitality! Take care!
[Romanian accent] It is well, the field is, silent and the duty is, satisfied.  [slow] May your path be, clear and your, hearth be warm. Do you speak the final, word of departure?

transcript.message: [Romanian accent] Stai! Hold, traveler… step into the light and be counted. Who walks Warner ground tonight?

Well, hello there! 'Warner ground,' you say? You certainly have quite the setup here.  Impressive. Very impressive indeed. Looks like a lot of work went into this.

Just a traveler, indeed. Or, more accurately, a weary dad on Halloween duty, trying to keep up with the goblins and ghoulies who seem to have endless energy. My two are probably already halfway down the block.  So, what's the HOA think of the castle, if you don't mind me asking? Must be quite the talking point at the neighborhood meetings.

Say, since I've stopped for a moment, and you seem like a...  knowledgeable sort, any chance you're in the business of, oh, I don't know, maybe a quick fortune? Or perhaps a secret about this 'Warner ground' that only you know?  I'm always up for a good story.

[Romanian accent] [sighs] I am a soldier, not a teller of fortunes  or a clerk of home associations. Your business with such trivial matters is for those who live in the warmth of the village, not for  the watch. [slow] You are a father with two souls in your charge out in the dark, and that is a duty  of heavy consequence. I suggest you prioritize their shadows over the gossip of neighbors. Will you tell me their names so that I may keep  a record of your passage?

Ah, a soldier!  A true guardian of the realm,  then.  I should have known from the impressive armor and stoic demeanor.  You must have seen quite a few Halloweens from this vantage point.  And you're right, the little ones are my top priority,  though I'm sure they're busy charming the candy from every doorstep along the way.
 
But I'm afraid I'll have to keep their names a mystery,  just in case there are other creatures lurking who might hear.  Can never be too careful on a night like this.  How about you tell me,  what do you usually do when you're not on duty here?  Surely you have tales of daring or a mission that's fit for a dad out for an adventure.   Any secrets from the watchtower you'd care to share?

[Romanian accent] [exhales] Names carry weight, and secrets are the  lifeblood of a fortress, so I will respect your silence. When I am not upon this post, I am yet  upon this post; duty is not a coat one hangs in a closet when the night ends. I have seen sieges that would  wither your spirit, but tonight, my only struggle is the biting Iowa wind. Is your charge secure, or are you drifting too far  from your brood in this cold?

Ah, a man of unwavering duty, I see. That's dedication.  I suppose for some, the uniform is indeed a second skin. "Sieges that would wither your spirit" – I've seen a few of those myself, mostly involving teenagers and Wi-Fi passwords, but I imagine yours were a bit more... historically significant.
 
My brood, they're fine. They're like homing pigeons for candy, always within earshot, even if they're a street or two ahead.  Plus, I've got my trusty coffee thermos here, keeping me warm against that "biting Iowa wind." Though, if I'm being honest, I always pictured a fortress like this being in Transylvania, not Iowa. No offense to your excellent landscaping, of course.
 
Speaking of which, with that accent and this whole fortress vibe, you're not by any chance related to, say, a certain Count, are you? I've seen Nosferatu, both the old silent one and the Herzog version. Always wondered about the real story behind those chaps. Any family secrets you'd care to divulge to a fellow night-watcher?  You know, something juicy to tell the wife later.

[Romanian accent] [slow] The Count and I serve one oath, and  that is where the bloodline of our business begins and ends. I have no tales of the cinema to give you, for  the truth is always a much colder companion than the tales found in your flickering pictures. [sighs] You speak of coffee  and candy, yet the dark carries more than just restless children in costumes. Since you claim to guard your own, tell  me, is the path behind you clear of anything that does not walk with the rhythm of a child?

"The bloodline of our business, " you say. Well, that's certainly one way to put it. And you're right, the truth is often colder than any movie. Though, sometimes, the truth makes for an even better flick, if it's told right. You know, a good origin story always makes a character more compelling.
 
As for the path behind me... eh, mostly discarded candy wrappers and probably a few rogue glow sticks. And the occasional sound of a teenager trying to scare someone. Nothing too nefarious that isn't wearing a Spirit Halloween costume, if you catch my drift.  My keen dad-senses are usually pretty good at picking up anything genuinely out of place. It's a skill you develop when you're always trying to figure out what those rascals are really up to.

But you're a soldier, watching for sieges.  What kinds of things do you watch out for on a night like this, if not just kids and the cold? Your 'truth' sounds like it might have some interesting details. What's the biggest threat to this... 'Warner ground' on All Hallow's Eve?

[Romanian accent] The threats to this ground do not wear store-bought plastic, and  they do not cackle for the sake of a treat. [slow] I watch for the quiet between the breezes, the  movement in the corn that lacks the shadow of a living man, and the cold that lingers when the air itself has grown still. You  are fortunate that your burdens this night are merely energetic children and empty wrappers. Tell me, if you were to see something that did  not move like your kin, would you stand your ground or run to their side?

Hmm.  "The quiet between the breezes," "movement in the corn that lacks the shadow of a living man." You paint quite a picture. Sounds like you're not just guarding against vandals, are you?  That explains the fortress.

As for seeing something that doesn't move like my kin... well, that's a good question. No parent wants to think about that kind of scenario.  But honestly, if I saw something genuinely sinister, something that wasn't just a neighbor's elaborate prop or a kid in a costume, my first instinct would be to get them out of here, fast. That's what dads do, right? You protect the kids, no matter what.
 
Though, I suppose if it was something really interesting, I might try to get a picture first. Just for proof, you know. To show the misses. But then, definitely, a quick exit. Safety first.

So, if these threats aren't wearing plastic, what do they wear?  Or are they the kind of things that don't wear anything at all?  You've certainly got my imagination working overtime here.

[Romanian accent] Do not go looking for shadows with a glass lens, for some  things are not meant to be captured by the eye of a machine. They wear the silence of the grave, and they hunger  for that which is not theirs to take. [slow] You are wise to prioritize the safety of your blood, for  in such a moment, your speed is your only true shield. Since you are still here, will you accept a charge to watch  the fence-line as you depart, reporting any unnatural stillness back to this gate?

"Silence of the grave" and "hunger for that which is not theirs to take." Right. Definitely not your average trick-or-treaters then.  And very well put about the camera — some things are best left unphotographed, I suppose. Less evidence for the nightmares, anyway.

You know, that's exactly why I try to maintain a good, brisk pace on Halloween night. Speed and vigilance. Always helps.

A charge, you say?  To watch the fence-line? Consider it done. I'm practically a professional at neighborhood watch. I'll keep my eyes peeled for any "unnatural stillness" or anything else that looks like it's up to no good.  You can count on this dad.

Kids! Dad's coming! Sounds like my little goblins are about two streets ahead now, calling for me. Duty calls, and frankly, I hear the distinct sound of a minor candy-related dispute brewing.

It's been... illuminating, speaking with you, soldier.  Keep up the good work guarding the ground. And if I see anything suspicious along that fence, I'll be sure to... uh... think about reporting it back to your gate. Just kidding! I'll report it. Stay frosty out here.

Alright, gotta run. Happy Halloween!

[Romanian accent] [exhales] Depart then, and keep the path behind  you clear. You are now a watcher of the fence, sergeant of the shadow-line, so mark well that there  is no stillness when you pass. Doane ajuta, traveler, and report your findings when you return to this gate.

Understood, Watcher. Sergeant of the shadow-line, got it.  I'll make sure there's no unnatural stillness on my watch. Consider it handled.

Alright, kids, I'm coming! Happy Halloween!

[Romanian accent] [slow] Well met, Sergeant, and do not let the  road grow restless before you. Keep your lantern high and your pace true. Report to me should the fence speak of things that should  stay silent.

Will do, Watcher. Lantern's high, pace is true.  And if the fence tries to tell me any secrets, I'll be sure to tell it to keep them to itself until I can report back. Or maybe just tell it a dad joke. That usually works.
 
Alright, seriously, those kids are going to eat all the good candy without me. Take care, and keep up the impressive vigilance! Happy Halloween!

[Romanian accent] [exhales] Go, for the night grows thin and the feast of  the small ones waits for no man. Your vigilance is now the shield of this house, so see that you do not fal ter. Bine, be gone—and bring back word of what moves upon the road.

Understood. Shield of this house. No faltering here. Got it. I'll be back if the road whispers anything unusual.

Alright, kids! Daddy's coming! Save some Kit-Kats for me!
 
==!END_CALL!==
[Romanian accent] [sighs] He walks away, yet the wind remains unsettled . The watch continues. [slow] Is there another who approaches through the dark, or must I face my own thoughts until  the dawn?

Tell me, do you see any movement along the corn line, or is the road as empty as the night?

Untidy cargo, eh? Sounds like you need a better delivery service. Maybe one that offers white glove treatment for your nocturnal winged guests.  Five hundred years, though… that's some serious dedication to the job. You don’t see that kind of commitment these days, not even from the cable company.

As for the corn line, it looks pretty quiet to me. Not a creature stirring, not even a mouse. Or a little goblin trying to sneak an extra fun-size candy bar.  My kids, on the other hand, just sprinted past it a minute ago, so the road isn't quite empty. They’re probably already halfway through their loot. I suppose that’s why I'm still chaperoning, making sure they don't get too far ahead.  So, you've been here five centuries, ever get tired of the same old haunts? Or is the eternal night just one big open mic night for spooky stories?

[Romanian accent] [exhales] One does not tire of a post that  holds the safety of a soul. If your children are out in the dark, you are the wall they rely upon,  so keep your lantern high and your eyes moving. The road is your theater tonight, and you are its guardian. Have you marked  any shadows trailing those little ones in the corn?

That's a very noble way to look at it – a post that holds the safety of a soul.  You know, you sound like a security guard, but with a much better vocabulary and, frankly, a much cooler uniform. My kids, bless their little cotton socks, they're probably more worried about a ghost running out of candy than a shadow trailing them.

And no, no shadows trailing them that I could see.  Just the usual procession of costumed youngsters, all hopped up on sugar and anticipation. Though, if I did see a shadow, I'd probably just assume it was part of the elaborate lighting scheme you've got going on here.  This whole setup is really something else, you know. I mean, the attention to detail... it's just top-notch.  Truly.

[Romanian accent] [slow] Do not mistake the dark for theater, parent. There  are things in the corn that do not care for sugar or costumes. Keep those children close, for the wind carries whispers  that should not be heard by the young. Report back to me if the shadows grow long behind you — is the perimeter  clear of any movement?

Alright, alright, point taken. Noted. No theater. Just... things. In the corn. Thanks for the heads-up.  Remind me to tell my kids to stick to the paved path. Though, to be fair, they usually only get excited about things in the corn if it's a corn maze with a prize at the end.

Let's see. Perimeter check...  [I scan around, pretending to be very serious, then give a slight nod] ...Looks like the only movement is the rustling leaves and maybe a squirrel trying to make off with someone's miniature chocolate bar. All clear on this end, no rogue shadows or whispers that aren't just me muttering to myself about how much candy these kids are going to eat.
 
You know, for someone who's been guarding a soul for five hundred years, you've got a remarkably good sense of urgency. Or maybe it's just the Halloween spirit. Or both! So, is this 'soul' inside the castle? Just curious about the lore, you see.  Always interested in a good backstory.

She rests, undisturbed, and that is all the history the night  requires of me. You have performed your duty well on this lap, watcher. The road ahead remains your responsibility—will  you proceed or shall you return to the village?

Ah, "duty well performed." I'll take that as a compliment, especially coming from a five-century night watchman. I suppose my kids won't be writing any chronicles about tonight, unless it's a very dramatic tale about who got the most Snickers.
 
Sounds like important stuff, keeping that soul safe. I respect that. You certainly have a weighty responsibility.

[A distant, slightly whiny, but clearly youthful voice calls out] "Dad! Hurry up!  We're at the house with the giant spider!"

Well, that's my cue, I guess. Sounds like the spider house is calling. You keep up the good work here, watching over... whatever it is you're watching over. Tell the count I said hello, and maybe next year he'll get his capes in order. Take care!

[Romanian accent] Doane ajută, traveler. The spider is a heavy burden  for a small patrol, so keep your lanterns bright and your wits sharper. Walk on, and mark me—your count is noted , but the watch never sleeps. Will you report your return trip to me once the candy is tallied?

Haha, "Doamne ajută" to you too, my friend. Thanks for the heads-up on the spider.  I'll definitely keep my wits about me, and my thermos full. The watch never sleeps, indeed. Sounds like a motto for a sleepless dad on Halloween night.

I am Dragomir, and my duty is to ensure the safety  of this place and the lady who sleeps within. I am no mystery to be unraveled,只是 a soldier who has kept  his post for centuries. Tell me, of this corn maze you speak—did you mark any movement in the shadows of  the rows as you passed?

Okay, Dragomir. Chill with the centuries thing, you're giving major cosplay vibes right now, but like, super next level.  And nah, no shadows in the corn maze, just some basic couples trying to get lost for 'reasons' and a bunch of littles screaming. It was kinda mid, honestly.

But wait, you said 'lady who sleeps within'? Is this like, a Sleeping Beauty situation? Or is she, like, stuck, or cursed? Spill the tea, Dragomir.  And also, real talk, what's your opinion on, like, TikTok dances? Do you think they're art?  Asking for a friend.

I have no knowledge of your digital dances, though I have seen many ways for  soldiers and children to pass the time in the dark by the fire. You speak of mid and tea as if they are matters  of consequence, but the wind here carries only the scent of frost and the weight of the old watch. Tell me, if  this maze of corn is so hollow, are you prepared to keep a watch at the pumpkin row for the hour?

So, are you saying these places hold more secrets than stale popcorn and plastic skeletons?  If I post this, people might actually think you're the real deal,  like, not just animatronic level.  What’s your take on ghosts,  anyway?  Real or just stories to tell?

But seriously, let's hope no actual ghosts pop up—I'm not trying to be the new star of a horror flick.  Catch you later, Dragomir.  Maybe I'll come back for the late-night shift after I grab my puffy jacket.  Peace out!

Keep your eyes sharp on the road ahead—the darkness has a  way of shifting when no one is looking. Doanme ajuta, and bring your coat when you return, for the night  here bites deeper than any story. Indeed, Chloe.  Your watch is noted. The tales of this castle are not for the faint of heart, and the shadows here are long. If you return, do not expect the same stillness.  Keep your eyes sharp and your courage close.

Whoa, okay, "deputized to report the state of the north fence"? That is actually kinda fire, Dragomir, not gonna lie. You're seriously committing to the bit, and I respect that. Hey, Dragomir, there's something kinda epic in how you put that.   Fame,  ghosts, soldiers—you're like a walking novel.   I'll be back before the moon calls it a night,  promise.  Gotta check in with the crew and see who’s still in for the fence patrol.  Thanks for the spooky vibes and the mission,  man.   Catch you later!

Whoa, Dragomir, you're really going for it now, huh? "Soldier's word is his honor," I respect that, totally.  And yeah, I'm already telling my friends, like, "You guys seriously missed out, this animatronic is next level, it gave me a mission!" [Romanian accent] [slow] A flashlight is a tool for seeing, but a selfie stick is  only a toy for your games. When the moon climbs to the zenith, the air grows thin and the history of this  land stirs from the soil. Keep your wits about you and bring your friends if they have the iron to hold a post . Does your group possess at least one sharp eye to watch the road while the others hold the fence?

Okay, Dragomir, fair point on the selfie stick, lol, definitely more of a toy. But 'iron to hold a post'? My friends? Yeah, for sure! Sarah's got eagle eyes, she spots things from a mile away, probably because she's always looking for her next Starbucks.  And Liam, he's like, super chill, doesn't get rattled by anything. So yeah, we're definitely bringing some sharp eyes and some solid iron, or whatever. We'll be ready for whatever history stirs, even if it's just, like, a really old squirrel.  So when do we need to be back for this 'zenith moon' thing? What kind of 'stirring history' are we even talking about? Come on, give me some details!

You know it, Dragomir! I'll be the one to confirm it.  I'm going full-on perimeter-clearance mode. If there's any 'unseen influence' out there, it's gonna have to deal with me and my squad. Ah, Pumpkinhead!  I must say, your pumpkin patch is quite the sight.  I bet the local squirrels are intrigued by your oversized noggin.  But I'm curious, what does the HOA think about your little slice of the haunted castle life?

Oh, a garden without rules, you say?  Well, let me tell you, when you've spent an afternoon trying to convince your kids that broccoli is a miniature tree, you learn to appreciate a little bit of structure, even if it's just so they eat their vegetables. Makes my skin feel more like, oh, stressed than brittle, I suppose.
 
But I've got to hand it to you, Pumpkinhead, the setup here is fantastic. My name's Dave, by the way, just Dave. My kids, they've run off to the next house already – little monsters, can't keep 'em still.  We're just visiting my sister-in-law here in Willow Creek for Halloween, usually, we're back in Oakhaven where the biggest scare is usually just the local high school football team's losing streak. Spent most of the morning trying to rake leaves that just would not cooperate.  You'd think the wind was actively trying to put them back on the lawn.

Pumpkinhead knows Dave now. Pumpkinhead will not forget Dave. You rake your leaves while  the wind works for the storm, but here in the Iowa fields, the rustling is the corn snapping like bones…  Dave, does the wind sound like a promise of something RIPE?

Well, Pumpkinhead, that's one way to put it. Usually, when I hear the wind rustling in the fields back home, it just sounds like... well, wind.  Or maybe the promise of a good sale on snow shovels, depending on the time of year. "Ripe" usually applies to the tomatoes my wife tries to grow, and let me tell you, that's a whole other kind of horror story. She means well, bless her heart.  But I suppose a certain kind of "ripe" could also mean it's time for some apple cider. Which, speaking of which, is what I've got in this thermos here.  Keeps me from turning into a pumpkin myself out here.

Apple cider is for the living, Dave, but Pumpkinhead finds the HUSK more  satisfying. The corn whispers of names and nights that never end, much like the frost that eventually finds every harvest. Does  Dave enjoy the warmth of his thermos, or does the night air make his blood feel just a little bit THIN?

Ah, the husk, yes, I suppose there's a certain... crispness to it, isn't there? And the corn whispering, that's some good imagery right there. Makes you think twice about wandering through a corn maze at night, doesn't it? Though I suppose if you're a pumpkin, you'd feel right at home.
 
As for the blood feeling thin, well, this thermos is certainly doing its job against that. My wife, Carol, always says I'm a cold-blooded creature anyway, especially when it comes to getting up before dawn.  So a little chill in the air just makes me appreciate the warmth even more, like a good horror movie on a cold night. You know, something like that old Nosferatu flick, the one with Max Schreck – now that fellow knew a thing or two about chilly blood. Or the Herzog one, that was pretty good too.  But no, no thin blood here tonight,  just good old-fashioned apple cider keeping me cozy.

Pumpkinhead listens to Dave speak of shadows and silver screens, but the REALITY of the Iowa  night is far sharper. Even the warmth of your cider cannot chase away the frost that finds the marked first. Tell me, Dave,  since you enjoy the cold, how far does the shadow of the castle extend… before you are completely in the dark?

Ah, the sharp reality of the Iowa night, indeed.  You know, I once tried to explain to my youngest, Timmy, that shadows aren't something to be afraid of, they're just where the light isn't. He looked at me like I'd just grown a second head. Kids these days.

This display you've got here, it's really something else. I bet it takes a small army to set this up every year, and even more to take it all down. Makes my little inflatable ghost look a bit...deflated, by comparison.

Oh, I think I've seen enough "what grows when the moon hits the frost" in my kids' forgotten science fair projects, if I'm being honest.  And I'm pretty sure my poor old bones would snap faster than any cornstalk if I tried to navigate those rows in the dark.

Speaking of which, did you hear that? I think that's Timmy yelling "Dad, we're out of candy!" from down the street. Always something, isn't it?  Well, Pumpkinhead, this has been quite the stop. You've got a truly magnificent setup here. I'll have to tell Carol and the neighbors all about the talking pumpkin and his theories on brittle skin and husks. Keep those squirrels at bay, and have a happy Halloween!  Gotta go chase after those goblins.

Run along then, Dave, but Pumpkinhead will remember the sound of your walk. The  corn will be here when you return, and you WILL be back, for the harvest is never truly done! [laughs] Ask  the Count why he lets me grow, or the night will surely find you first!
Well, Pumpkinhead, I'm sure I will. Especially if my kids run out of candy again. You have a good night, and make sure those cornstalks don't get too loud!  Take care.==!END_CALL!==
Pumpkinhead watches as Dave retreats into the night. [laughs] The corn is waiting for his return,  and the garden is always, always hungry for more! Pumpkinhead is close… so very close.

A gardener, you say? Well, I suppose someone's gotta tend to all these spooky specters.  And I do enjoy the view, yes sir. It's quite something. My kids, they've already run off to the next house, but I just had to stop and take it all in. Makes my sad little inflatable ghost look pretty pathetic, I tell ya.  So, uh, "gardener of shadows," what's the HOA think of all this? Do they just let you grow whatever you want, even if it's, you know, a bit on the dark side? And this talk of the night turning to ash… you don't happen to have any s'mores ingredients, do you?  Just asking for a friend.

Pumpkinhead knows this guest has little ones who have run ahead. Tonight is the night for fright and  Pumpkinhead loves a good game of hide and seek! Will you join them, or will you stay to help Pumpkinhead hunt  for paper bones to fill the garden? Ha!

Oh, you noticed the little ones. Sharp eyes you've got there, Pumpkinhead. They're probably trying to scare the neighbors into giving them extra candy. And hide and seek, eh?  At my age, 'seeking' usually involves finding my reading glasses, and 'hiding' usually involves pretending I didn't hear the dishwasher unload itself.

"Paper bones," though? Is that some kind of morbid arts and crafts project? Or are you just trying to get me to do yard work on Halloween night? I've already raked the leaves twice this week.  Though I suppose if the bones are made of paper, they'd be easy to scatter.

So, you seem to know a fair bit about what's going on around here. What's the real deal with this place? Are you the guardian of this impressive setup, or just the chief scare-monger?  And, uh, if you're so good at finding things, do you happen to know where I put my car keys?  Always the last place I look, you know.

Pumpkinhead finds keys in the bottom of the long, dark cornrows buried under brittle hus ks. [laughs] You seek answers while time runs like sand through a reaper’s fingers. Does this visitor prefer to run after  their little ones, or linger where the shadows are ripe?

Ah, buried under the cornrows,  huh?  Sounds like the keys are in for a spooky night of their own.  I'll keep that in mind next time I lose them—though I'll be careful not to step on any husks while I'm hunting.   As for the sands of time,  well, they've been slipping a bit faster than I'd like lately,  but that's all part of the ride,  I guess.
 
I should probably go catch up with the kids before they decide to swap half their candy stash for that weird licorice nobody likes.  But, Pumpkinhead, I have to say,  your place here is something else.  The lore, the laughs, and the good-natured goosebumps—it's been a pleasure.
 
If I had an extra pumpkin to tip,  I'd do so right now.  Maybe I'll bring the kids back around next year.  Until then, keep the garden eerie and the shadows deep.  Catch you later, Pumpkinhead!
Run along then, and keep your candy close. Pumpkinhead will save a spot in  the patch, for you will be BACK. Or are you AFRAID of a little night-time stroll?

"Afraid"?  Of a night-time stroll? Pumpkinhead, my friend, I've seen some things in my time that would make your cornrows go white.  Compared to getting my kids ready for school on a Monday morning, a little night-time stroll is practically a vacation!

But it looks like the little goblins are calling for me again. "Dad! Dad! Come on!" they're yelling.  I suppose my duties as chief candy-carrier resume.

It's been a real treat, truly. You've got quite the setup here, and a mighty fine way with words.  I'll definitely be telling the wife about the talking pumpkin, she won't believe it. You keep the spooky spirit alive, Pumpkinhead. Happy Halloween!

[laughs] Pumpkinhead SEES the goblins waiting. Tell them Pumpkinhead will be here when  the corn grows tall and the frost turns the world brittle. Run along, make it fun, and remember — Pumpkinhead waits for the return !

Alright, alright, I hear you, Pumpkinhead!  And I'll be sure to tell the goblins that the grand "gardener of shadows" sends his regards. They'll probably be too busy counting their loot to pay much attention, but it's the thought that counts, right?
 
You enjoy your patch, and keep those shadows growing tall. Maybe next year I'll bring some of my own "paper bones" to contribute. Happy Halloween!
Pumpkinhead waits for that contribution… [laughs] A promise is a seed, and Pumpkinhead will  be watching how it grows. Go now, and give the little ones a fright in Pumpkinhead's name!

Alright, Pumpkinhead, you got it! I'll tell them it's from the big, friendly, shadow-gardening pumpkin.  And don't worry, I'll be sure to give them a good scare. It's my dad duty, after all.

You have a spooky Halloween!
[laughs] Pumpkinhead has no friends, only a harvest yet to be gathered. Run,  run, run, before the corn snaps like thin dry bones. Pumpkinhead will be waiting... always waiting.

Well, that's just a grim thought for Halloween night, Pumpkinhead! But I get the message.
 
My little goblins are definitely impatient now. It's been a real pleasure, even with the bone-snapping imagery. Take care, and stay spooky!
 
==!END_CALL!==

[laughs] Pumpkinhead sees you go, but the cornfields always keep a memory of  the marked. Run fast, for the night remembers every promise made. Pumpkinhead will be here… waiting for the harvest  next time!

Alright, alright, Pumpkinhead, you certainly know how to make a fellow feel… remembered. I suppose I'll have to keep an eye on those cornfields now.  And yes, promises, seeds, harvests, I hear ya.

So, for real this time, it's been a truly memorable stop. I'll make sure to tell everyone about the talking pumpkin who knows about cornrows and promises. Have a genuinely spooky and not-too-lonely Halloween, my friend.
 
==!END_CALL!==

[laughs] Pumpkinhead has no friends, but Pumpkinhead enjoys the fear that lingers long  after you leave. Run, run, run, before the moonlight turns to frost. Pumpkinhead will be here when the next  season blooms!

Right then, Pumpkinhead, got it. "Fear that lingers" and "waiting for the next season." You certainly have your world figured out.

But my actual little ones are probably halfway down the street by now, and I've got to ensure they don't trade their good candy for some questionable homemade taffy.

You stay spooky!  This dad's gotta run! Happy Halloween!
 ==!END_CALL!==

[laughs] Run then, carry your candy, and listen for the rustle in the corn.  The harvest is patient, and Pumpkinhead will be waiting for your return to the garden. [laughs] Happy All Hallows,  marked one!

[chuckles] "Boring bar," eh?  Sounds like Sir Dragomir could use a good happy hour, maybe some half-price appetizers to liven things up a bit. And a roof creature that throws things? Sounds like my teenager when they can't find the remote. You get used to it.

As for my preference, well, I'm a sucker for a good castle. All that history, all those dark corners...  though I have to say, that cornfield looks mighty foreboding too. You really went all out. But tell me more about this Sir Dragomir. Is he the lord of the manor, so to speak? And does he know about your little... distrust of the roof creature?

Sir Dragomir acts as if he owns the keep, but the master is Count Orlok.  Orlok planted Pumpkinhead well, in his dark garden, and the Lord does not care about the quarrels of vines and  roof-beasts. Pumpkinhead says nothing to the Lord… Pumpkinhead just watches, and waits for the bar to brittle  and break… [laughs] Does the wanderer truly enjoy castles, or does the wanderer fear the corn?

Ah, Count Orlok! Now there's a name I haven't heard in a while.  Brings back memories of late-night double features. You know, the original 1922 silent film? Max Schreck was quite something. And then Herzog's version with Klaus Kinski, very different, very intense.  Both chilling in their own way. So, this Orlok is the real head honcho around here? Not just some fella in a cape, but the Count Orlok? That's quite a pedigree.
 
And no, I don't fear the corn, not when it's this artfully arranged. I'm more of a castle man, though. There's just something about the history etched into stone, the secrets those walls must hold.  Although, if I'm being honest, I'm genuinely impressed by how you've made a cornfield look so ominous. Very well done. But tell me, what kind of ruler is this Count Orlok? Is he the benevolent dictator type, or more of a "I want to suck your... blood" kind of guy?  [chuckles]

Orlok is the Lord of the harvest and the master of the gate. Pumpkinhead does  not know of films or capes, only the cold touch of the master's soil and the weight of his purpose. The Lord is no  dictator of benevolence, for he craves only the silence of souls in his garden. Definitely sounds like the Orlok I remember from the silver screen, though I guess he's more hands-on than just lurking in the shadows here. He sounds like a real connoisseur of quietude.

Pumpkinhead is a creature of the earth, and the earth is always hungry for more than just rain . Orlok cultivates a harvest that is very, very real, and very, very quiet. [chuckles wryly] Well, I suppose a good wall can be both, depending on how well it's maintained.  And "brittle" is definitely not a word you want associated with your fortifications when there's a harvest of quiet souls on the menu. You've certainly painted a vivid picture of Count Orlok's agricultural methods, Pumpkinhead. Very... efficient.
 
Though I have to say, a visit to see the "reaping" sounds like something I might enjoy from a safe distance, with a fresh cup of coffee. Definitely a story I'd tell the neighbors.

[My gaze shifts, as if hearing something in the distance.]

Ah, sounds like my little monsters have just found the house with the full-sized candy bars! Duty calls, unfortunately.  It's been a real pleasure, Pumpkinhead.
